title: Facile fabrication and evaluation of novel composites for antimicrobial and anticancer applications
desc: Novel geopolymer/zeolite/lignin (abbreviated as GZL) and geopolymer/zeolite/lignin/chitosan (abbreviated as GZLC) composites were successfully fabricated and evaluated for antimicrobial and anticancer applications. The synthesized composites were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). XRD confirmed the coexistence of amorphous geopolymer/lignin phases and crystalline sodium aluminum silicate hydrate zeolite, while the appearance of chitosan-related peaks verified successful chitosan incorporation. EDX detected nitrogen in GZLC, further confirming the presence of chitosan. FE-SEM revealed that chitosan incorporation produced a more integrated and film-like morphology. FTIR confirmed the coexistence of aluminosilicate, lignin, and chitosan functional groups. Biological evaluation showed selective antibacterial activity, especially against Gram-positive bacteria, where GZLC produced inhibition zones of 14 and 13 mm against Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, respectively. No antifungal activity was observed against Aspergillus flavus or Candida albicans. The anticancer assay against HCT-116 colon cancer cells showed concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with GZLC exhibiting the strongest activity and the lowest IC50 value of 111.28 ± 9.42 µg/mL. These findings highlight GZLC as a promising multifunctional bioactive composite for biomedical applications.
